The Green Jacket

The Tournament

Welcome to The Dadchelor

Each year, a band of brothers — husbands, fathers, and self-proclaimed single-digit handicappers — converge upon a storied Michigan golf course for the most prestigious tournament no one outside their group has ever heard of.

What began as a trip between friends has evolved into a full-blown institution: complete with a champion's jacket, official tournament records, player announcements read aloud on the first tee, and the kind of competitive fire that only comes from years of shared friendship, trash talk, and the occasional three-putt.

About The Dadchelor

History · Traditions · The Spirit of the Game

Our Story

A Brotherhood Forged in Fairways

The Dadchelor Invitational was born from a simple idea: that a group of lifelong friends — now husbands, fathers, and reluctant adults — deserved one weekend a year to reclaim their inner competitor, swing some clubs, and remind one another exactly who the alpha golfer of the group really is.

What started as a casual Michigan golf trip has grown into a full-fledged institution. Each year, before a single ball is struck, every competitor is formally announced on the first tee — their accomplishments, accolades, and deeply questionable life decisions read aloud for the entertainment of the assembled field.

The champion earns the green jacket, the right to select the following year's course, and bragging rights that must be surrendered at the next edition.

The tournament has been held at some of Michigan's finest golf destinations, with the field growing in size and competitive intensity with each passing year.

And then came 2026.

The eighth edition marks the dawn of a new chapter — The Modern Era of The Dadchelor Invitational. For the first time, players do not merely compete for Lil and Big Peen honors, for Look Good and Feel Good accolades, or for the right to have their biography read aloud on the first tee. They now contend for something greater: the title of Champion Golfer of the Year.

The Champion Golfer of the Year is a man who will be immortalized for all time — a man who has earned the right, proudly and without apology, to ask the question that echoes across every fairway, every green, and every 19th hole deliberation: "Who's your Daddy?"

The Modern Era is ushered in partly through the power of artificial intelligence — bringing full website integration, live scoring through Bogey Golf, and a rich digital tournament experience that would have been unthinkable in the early editions. The Dadchelor has grown up. The game has changed. The stakes have never been higher.

Sacred Traditions

🎙️

The First Tee Announcements

Before play begins, each competitor is formally announced — their biography read aloud on the first tee. Accuracy is aspirational.

🏌️

The Opening Tee Shot

The defending champion hits first. No warm-up. No excuses. All eyes on you.

⚔️

Singles Matchups

Should the agenda allow, matchups are determined by team captains following the penultimate round (preferably surrounded by trash talking from both teams). Any player is permitted to call out a member from the other team as a matter of rivalry, subject to the approval of team captains.

🎽

The Jacket Ceremony

The outgoing champion formally presents the green jacket to the new champion. A handshake, a photo, and a speech is required.

📍

Champion's Course Selection

The defending champion selects the following year's venue. This power is to be wielded wisely — and usually isn't.

Est. 2026

The Modern Era

2026 · The Dadchelor Enters a New Age

🏆

Champion Golfer of the Year

For the first time in Dadchelor history, players compete not just for team glory, jacket rights, or first-tee bragging rights — but for an individual title that stands above all others. The Champion Golfer of the Year earns the right to ask one question, loudly and without apology:

"Who's your Daddy?"

The defending champion earns the privilege to choose the food and beverage menu at the following year's tournament, and pay for said menu at his own expense.

⚔️

The Ryder Cup Format

Team Look Good vs Team Feel Good. Four rounds across two days. Fourball, Scramble, and Individual Match Play. The team with the most points lifts the Dadchelor Cup. Every stroke, every putt, every conceded hole counts toward both the team battle and the individual race.

🤖 Powered by the Modern Age

The Modern Era arrives partly through the power of artificial intelligence — bringing full website integration, live scoring via Bogey Golf, and a rich digital tournament experience that would have been unthinkable in the early editions. The Dadchelor Invitational has grown up. And the game will never be the same.

The Legend

Tournament Lore

The Honors

Lil Peen & Big Peen

Lil Peen and Big Peen were the original team names for the first two Dadchelors — irreverent, perfectly on brand, and exactly what you'd expect. They were eventually rebranded to Look Good and Feel Good to be more palatable to potential trip sponsors. We never got the sponsors. We kept the names anyway.

The First Tee

The Announcements

Before a single ball is struck, the field assembles on the first tee. One by one, each competitor is formally announced — their accomplishments, their accolades, their life milestones, and their most deeply questionable decisions read aloud for the entertainment of everyone present. Accuracy is aspirational. The crowd does not always believe everything they hear. The competitor has no right of reply.

The Modern Era · 2026

Champion Golfer of the Year

The newest and highest individual honor in the tournament. Introduced in 2026 with the adoption of the Ryder Cup team format, the Champion Golfer of the Year is the player who accumulates the most personal points across all four rounds. He is not merely a winner. He is the man who, by right of conquest and personal excellence, has earned the eternal privilege of asking — loudly, proudly, and with full confidence — "Who's your Daddy?"

Tournament Courses

The Hallowed Grounds of The Dadchelor

Seven Years · Seven Venues

The Hallowed Grounds

2019 · Inaugural Edition

Treetops Resort

Gaylord, Michigan · September 13–15

Threetops Par-3
Threetops
Designed by Rick Smith · Par 27

America's #1 Par-3 course. Nine legendary short holes perched dramatically above Gaylord with views spanning 40 miles. Featured on ESPN's Par-3 Shootout from 1999–2006. In 2001, Lee Trevino made a hole-in-one here worth $1,000,000.

Championship Course
Black Lake Golf Club
Designed by Rees Jones · Onaway, MI

Consistently ranked among Michigan's finest, Black Lake is a championship layout cut through dense Northern Michigan forest along the shores of Black Lake. Rees Jones designed a course that rewards precision off the tee and demands a complete game.

Par 72 · 6,544 yards
The Tradition Course
Designed by Rick Smith · Treetops Resort

A classic Northern Michigan layout with generous fairways and a welcoming pace of play. The Tradition lives up to its name — reliable, scenic, and a perennial 4.5-star Golf Digest rated experience that rounds out any Treetops stay.

Par 72 · 6,832 yards
The Premier Course
Designed by Tom Fazio · Only Fazio in Michigan

The only Tom Fazio-designed course in Michigan. Known for dramatic elevation changes, bowl-shaped fairways that reward errant tee shots, and challenging greens. Golf Digest 4.5 stars since 1992. Premier by name, premier by nature.

Championship Course
Loon Golf Course
Gaylord, Michigan

A Northern Michigan staple with sweeping views and classic Gaylord-area terrain. The Loon is a fan favorite among golfers looking for an engaging round in one of Michigan's finest golf destinations.

📖 Stories from 2019
Share a memory — before it's lost to history
The inaugural edition. The tournament that started it all — but because we were living in the dark ages, pre-2026, pre-Claude, the results were never written down. Players speak in hushed tones of that first weekend in Gaylord. What happened at Threetops stays at Threetops. Or does it?

2020 · 2nd Edition

Boyne Highlands Resort

Harbor Springs, Michigan · September 11–13

Par 72 · 6,906 yards
Crooked Tree Golf Club
Harbor Springs, Michigan

Named for the distinctive Petoskey-area landmark, Crooked Tree is a beloved Harbor Springs layout featuring tree-lined fairways, pristine conditioning, and stunning views of the Little Traverse Bay region.

Par 72 · 7,179 yards
Donald Ross Memorial Course
Tribute to the Master · Boyne Highlands

A loving tribute to the legendary designer featuring replica holes from Ross's most celebrated courses — Pinehurst No. 2, Seminole, and Oakland Hills among them. Walking this course is a masterclass in classic American golf architecture.

Par 72 · 7,034 yards
Arthur Hills Course
Designed by Arthur Hills · Boyne Highlands

A signature Arthur Hills design winding through the natural terrain of Northern Michigan's rolling hills. Known for its dramatic elevation changes, generous landing areas, and well-protected greens demanding precise approach play.

Par 72 · 6,920 yards
The Heather Course
Boyne Highlands · Harbor Springs

The crown jewel of Boyne Highlands — a Robert Trent Jones Sr. design consistently ranked among Michigan's top five courses. The Heather has hosted PGA Section events and remains one of the most scenic rounds anywhere in the Midwest.

📖 Stories from 2020
Share a memory — before it's lost to history
Harbor Springs. Boyne Highlands. Four courses over three days. Whatever happened there is gone — lost to history like so many great stories told around the 19th hole. Some say there was a collapse on the back nine of the Donald Ross. Others dispute it. Nobody wrote anything down.

2021 · 3rd Edition

Treetops Resort & Otsego Club

Gaylord, Michigan · July 30 – August 1

Par 27 · America's #1
Threetops
Designed by Rick Smith · Par-3 Icon

A return engagement for the Dadchelor faithful. Threetops never gets old — nine holes of pure drama perched above the Gaylord valley. The scene of Lee Trevino's million-dollar ace in 2001.

Historic Course
The Tribute at Otsego Club
Otsego Club · Gaylord, Michigan

One of Michigan's hidden gems. The Tribute at Otsego Club is a classic layout steeped in Northern Michigan history, offering a beautifully traditional golf experience that stands in contrast to the modern resort tracks across Gaylord.

Par 72 · 6,832 yards
Premier Course
Designed by Tom Fazio · Treetops Resort

The only Tom Fazio design in Michigan returns for a second Dadchelor appearance. Dramatic elevation changes, precision required off the tee, and greens that demand your full attention on every approach.

Par 71 · 6,653 yards
Signature Course
Designed by Rick Smith · Treetops Resort

Ranked #2 Best of the Midwest by Golf Magazine. The Signature draws on Scottish and Irish links influences with visually threatening lines off the tee that open up with smart course management. Arguably the best-conditioned course at Treetops.

📖 Stories from 2021
Share a memory — before it's lost to history
A return to Gaylord. Treetops and Otsego. The third Dadchelor, and still — not a single result recorded. The scores, the drama, the winner's speech — all of it dissolved into northern Michigan air by Sunday evening.

2022 · 4th Edition · Most Ambitious Yet

Forest Dunes Golf Club

Roscommon, Michigan · August 26–28

🌀 Home of The Loop — the only reversible 18-hole golf course in the world, designed by Tom Doak
World's Only Reversible Course
The Loop — Red & Black Routings
Designed by Tom Doak · Top 50 Worldwide

Tom Doak's obsession with reversible British links became reality at Forest Dunes. The same 18 holes play as two completely different courses depending on direction — Red (counter-clockwise) and Black (clockwise). No. 2 today becomes No. 16 tomorrow. Consistently ranked Top 50 public courses in America.

Top 50 Public USATom DoakReversible
10-hole Short Course
Bootlegger Short Course
Designed by Keith Rhebb & Riley Johns

Named for the Purple Gang — a Detroit mafia family that ran a ranch on this property in the 1920s and 30s. Ten holes, 1,100 yards of pure fun. Two or three clubs, cold beverages, shoes optional. Golf as it should be at the end of a long day.

Championship Course
Dream Course
West Branch, Michigan

The Dream lives up to its name — a sweeping parkland layout carved through the northern Michigan forest with wide landing zones and undulating greens. Sister course to The Nightmare, carved out of 312 acres of hardwoods just west of downtown West Branch. No liquor license — BYOB is the only way.

Championship Course
Nightmare Course
West Branch, Michigan

The name says it all. The Dream's sister course, opened in 2003. Wide fairways belie a course with serious teeth — large undulating greens, strategic bunkering, and elevation changes that make every approach a decision. No liquor license. Bring your own.

Par 72 · 6,982 yards
The Fortress
Frankenmuth, Michigan

A fortress in name and in nature. Designed with dramatic bunkering and strategic water features, The Fortress in Frankenmuth demands respect from the first tee to the 18th green. A perennial Michigan top-25 rated course with a castle-inspired aesthetic.

📖 Stories from 2022
Share a memory — before it's lost to history
Forest Dunes. The Loop. Possibly the greatest setting in Dadchelor history. Whatever unfolded on the fairways of the Bootlegger, the Dream, the Nightmare, and the Fortress is known only to those who were there — and even they disagree on the details.

2023 · 5th Edition · Southern Swing

Ann Arbor & Northville

Southeast Michigan · August 5–6

Par 72 · Ypsilanti, MI
Eagle Crest Golf Club
Ypsilanti, Michigan · Arnold Palmer Design

An Arnold Palmer-designed championship course just outside Ann Arbor. Eagle Crest winds through mature oaks and wetlands with challenging bunkering and multi-tiered greens. A true test of the complete game close to home.

University of Michigan
Radrick Farms (Michigan Course)
Designed by Robert Trent Jones Sr. · U of M

The University of Michigan's historic championship course designed by Robert Trent Jones Sr. in 1964. Radrick Farms has hosted multiple Big Ten Championships and remains one of the most prestigious layouts in the state. Go Blue.

Par 72 · Northville, MI
Northville Hills Golf Club
Northville, Michigan

A parkland gem in suburban Detroit's finest golf corridor. Northville Hills features tree-lined fairways, strategically placed bunkers, and bentgrass greens that reward patience and accuracy. A fitting closer to the 2023 southern swing.

📖 Stories from 2023
Share a memory — before it's lost to history
Ann Arbor and Northville. Eagle Crest, Radrick Farms, Northville Hills. A fifth edition with no official record. The results exist only in memory — and memory, as any golfer knows, is a generous scorer.

2024 · 6th Edition

The Orchards Golf Club

Lake Orion, Michigan · August 23–24

Back-to-Back · Two Days
The Orchards Golf Club
Designed by Robert Trent Jones Jr. · Lake Orion

A Robert Trent Jones Jr. masterpiece consistently ranked among Michigan's top ten courses. The Orchards features dramatic elevation changes, pristine conditioning, and a layout that rewards course management over brute force. The 2024 Dadchelor doubled down — same course, two days, with completely different results on the board each time.

Michigan Top 10R.T. Jones Jr.Played Twice

2025 · 7th Edition

Tawas City & Au Gres

Lake Huron Shoreline, Michigan · August 22–24

East Tawas, Michigan
Red Hawk Golf Club
East Tawas, Michigan

A scenic challenge along Michigan's Lake Huron shoreline. Red Hawk Golf Club is a highly rated local gem featuring tight tree-lined fairways, well-maintained greens, and that unmistakable northern Michigan feel at a fraction of the resort price.

Au Gres, Michigan
Huron Breeze Golf & Country Club
Au Gres, Michigan · Lake Huron Region

Situated along the Lake Huron shoreline in Au Gres, Huron Breeze is a fan-favorite among Michigan golfers who value character over course rating. Expect a breezy round (literally and figuratively) with wide fairways and the kind of no-nonsense Michigan hospitality that keeps golfers coming back.

Par 72 · 6,982 yards
The Fortress
Frankenmuth, Michigan · Returns for 2025

The Fortress makes its second Dadchelor appearance after the 2022 Forest Dunes trip. If anything, the castle-like bunkering and demanding layout will feel even more familiar — and no less brutal — the second time around.

📖 Stories from 2025

Tawas. Au Gres. Red Hawk, Huron Breeze, The Fortress. The seventh and final edition before the Modern Era — and the last tournament lost to history. No records. No official champion. Only stories. Until now.
